Belz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Belz was the actual seat of the Belz Hasidic dynasty — one of the largest and most influential Hasidic movements in the world today, with hundreds of thousands of adherents worldwide. In 1843, the dynasty's founder, tzadik Sholom Rokeach (1783–1855), built the Great Synagogue of Belz in the town. The Jewish community, present from the early 15th century, suffered hunger and plague during the Khmelnytsky uprising of 1648–49, losing more than 200 people, and later peaked at 3,625 (60.2 percent of the town) in 1910. When the Red Army withdrew from Belz in October 1939, almost all local Jews fled; on June 2, 1942, about 1,000 Jews were deported to the Sobibór death camp, and roughly 500 more followed later that year. About 220 Jews returned to Belz after 1945.
